title: Common table expressions (CTEs)
description: A CTE, written with WITH, names a query so you can reference it later like a temporary table - it's often clearer than nesting a subquery inline. Using a CTE named `avg_price`, write a query that returns the `name` and `price` of every product priced above the average price of all products.
hints: WITH avg_price AS (SELECT AVG(price) AS value FROM products) defines a one-row, one-column result you can then treat like a table in the main query that follows it.
WITH avg_price AS (...) SELECT p.name, p.price FROM products p, avg_price WHERE p.price > avg_price.value.
expected_behavior: Returns name and price for products priced above the average - same result as the earlier subquery exercise, written as a CTE instead.
solution: WITH avg_price AS (SELECT AVG(price) AS value FROM products) SELECT p.name, p.price FROM products p, avg_price WHERE p.price > avg_price.value;
explanation: A CTE and an inline subquery can express exactly the same logic - the difference is readability (and, for a CTE referenced more than once, not repeating the same subquery over and over).
